classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two prices per orange by division and round to the nearest cent.

content.prompt: One store at the market advertises oranges at 15 for $\$2.00$ and another at 20 for $\$2.40$. Calculate the price per orange for each store (rounding correct to the nearest cent).

answer.short: First store: 13 cents per orange; second store: 12 cents per orange.
answer.worked:
First store:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost per orange}&=\$2.00\div15\\\text{Cost per orange}&=\$0.1333\ldots\\\text{Cost per orange}&\approx\$0.13\end{align*}$$
Second store:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cost per orange}&=\$2.40\div20\\\text{Cost per orange}&=\$0.12\end{align*}$$
The prices are 13 cents and 12 cents per orange respectively, correct to the nearest cent.
